The headline is already at the field tier: the substantive joint claim is two-sided \(O(h)\) lifting that preserves a fixed coded law exactly, followed by exact finite-sample whole-set coverage; computation is separately totalized only for the rational certifiable subclass. Under merely Lipschitz mechanisms and queries, linear mesh error is the natural field-rate order, while a sharper sampling rate cannot replace \(\omega_Q(r_n)\) without an endpoint-stability or margin assumption. The district-coupled response construction, exact feasibility/empty-output branch, and certified endpoint branch address the important elbows; improving constants would be local rather than material. The scope is appropriately limited to the fixed code, with unrestricted computation, unbinned-law coverage, polynomial runtime, the discrete bow model, and neural density all explicitly excluded from the headline. This supports field, not a higher tier, because the executable class is deliberately restrictive and neural endpoint density remains unresolved.

The note’s \(M_G\) is neither published anchor class. Zhang–Tian–Bareinboim require finite endogenous domains and use finite atomic exogenous canonical SCMs, whereas \(M_G\) permits continuous endogenous variables and imposes bounded-density continuous district noises, Lipschitz mechanisms, and independent rank variables. Their theorem transfers only distributional finite canonicalization to an all-categorical member’s counterfactual law; the canonical representative need not remain in \(M_G\), so it transfers neither class containment nor endpoint equality. [Zhang–Tian–Bareinboim](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/zhang22ab/zhang22ab.pdf)

Tan–Blanchet–Syrgkanis use independent canonical component latents, independent Gumbel categorical randomization, bounded supports, and Lipschitz structural/propensity functions; their quantitative neural approximation additionally imposes latent-support/distribution geometry. The note instead fixes district boxes with bounded Lebesgue densities and inverse-CDF ranks. Rank and Gumbel sampling overlap distributionally, and Tan’s Wasserstein approximation can transfer on the intersection satisfying their extra latent hypotheses, but it does not preserve a merely measurable finite code exactly and therefore cannot imply the note’s exact-feasibility residual or coverage claim. The writeup repeatedly and correctly disclaims containment. [Tan–Blanchet–Syrgkanis](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/7f9220f90cc85b0da693643add6618e6-Paper-Conference.pdf)

`lem:exact-rational-semialgebraic-decision` is honestly imported from Basu–Pollack–Roy, with the core giving the precise Sections 13.1 and 14.1 locator and the writeup supplying explicit attribution and bibliography. Exact sign determination and real-univariate sample representations over \(\mathbb Q\) support both feasibility and infeasibility; replaying a terminating exact computation gives a finite independently checkable transcript, with no unclaimed short-certificate or complexity guarantee. [Basu–Pollack–Roy](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-33099-2)

Finally, `oeq:neural-endpoint-density` is framed honestly: ordinary ReLU/Wasserstein approximation does not preserve exact membership in code-defined fibers for a merely measurable \(\kappa\), and unbounded architecture size prevents a fixed finite global near-extremality certificate. Resolving it would require genuinely stronger boundary-nullness/interior-feasibility and architecture-control assumptions, not a missed argument under the present hypotheses.

A forward-only replacement can prove coverage, but not a field-tier result: any actual SCM can be embedded in an abstract outer correspondence, so projecting an exact multinomial confidence region through that nonevaluable superset yields routine outer validity. With no reverse approximation, the relaxation may remain arbitrarily wider than the identified set as \(h\to0\); there is no substantive convergence rate or sharpness theorem. `thm:exact-whole-set-coverage` then reduces to exact multinomial projection plus deterministic set inclusion.
